boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named campus settings for solo work, group problem-solving, writing support, listening, and primary-source research. Confirm appointments or reservations where noted.

cards.title: Map the Problem in A04
cards.subtitle: Four-seat study room on Russell Library’s third floor
cards.notes: Reserve A04 for a small-group session, then use its whiteboard and supplied markers to diagram the problem before dividing the work.
cards.short_summary: A reservable four-person room equipped for collaborative visual work.
cards.evidence_claim: The official reservation page identifies A04 as a third-floor Russell Library study room with capacity for four, a whiteboard, markers, an eraser, power, and accessible space.
cards.access_notes: Check current availability and reserve through the official LibCal page. Green study-room maps are posted in library stairwells.

cards.title: Bring the Sticking Point
cards.subtitle: Tutoring and Supplemental Instruction in Russell Library
cards.notes: Arrive with one specific STEM or economics question and the work you have already tried, then use the posted drop-in tutoring window.
cards.short_summary: A staffed academic-support setting for focused course problem-solving.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU states that the Learning Center offers drop-in tutoring, Supplemental Instruction, success workshops, and bootcamps, primarily supporting core STEM and economics courses.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists the Learning Center on Russell Library’s second floor and posts drop-in tutoring hours; verify the current semester schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Work the Next Equation
cards.subtitle: Bottom-floor math support near Books & Brew
cards.notes: Take your current worksheet downstairs and isolate the first step you cannot justify before asking a tutor to walk through your reasoning.
cards.short_summary: A named library-based setting dedicated to working through mathematics.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Center’s official page identifies the Math Lab on Russell Library’s bottom floor, down the hall from Books & Brew.
cards.access_notes: Use is tied to Learning Center programming; consult the official page for current tutoring and semester availability.

cards.title: Revise with a Reader
cards.subtitle: Arts & Sciences Building, Room 2-56A
cards.notes: Book through WCOnline and bring a draft plus the assignment prompt; choose one revision priority to address during the consultation.
cards.short_summary: An appointment-based workspace for developing academic writing.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Writing Center page says it helps GCSU students build academic-writing confidence and skills and is located in Arts & Sciences Room 2-56A.
cards.access_notes: Appointments are scheduled through WCOnline from MyGCSU. The center asks students to cancel when unable to attend so the slot can be reused.

cards.title: Read the Record Up Close
cards.subtitle: Primary-source workspace in Special Collections & Galleries
cards.notes: Identify the collection you need before arriving, then contact library staff about research access and handling requirements for its materials.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-built room for examining archival sources under staff guidance.
cards.evidence_claim: A GCSU library announcement documents an expanded room for archival research within Russell Library’s renovated Special Collections & Galleries facilities.
cards.source_title: GCSU Library puts history on display in new Special Collections facilities
cards.access_notes: Research access and collection handling may require advance coordination with Special Collections & Galleries; confirm arrangements before visiting.

cards.title: Build History in Digital Form
cards.subtitle: Project workspace in Special Collections & Galleries
cards.notes: Define the source set and intended digital output first, then ask Special Collections staff whether the lab supports your proposed project.
cards.short_summary: A specialized environment for collaborative digital-history work.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU’s library announcement identifies a new digital humanities lab created for collaboration on digital-history projects in Special Collections & Galleries.
cards.source_title: GCSU Library puts history on display in new Special Collections facilities
cards.access_notes: The source documents the facility but not walk-in access. Contact Special Collections & Galleries to confirm project eligibility and scheduling.

cards.title: Prepare the Interview Record
cards.subtitle: Specialized history workspace in Russell Library
cards.notes: Draft an interview plan and consent workflow before contacting Special Collections staff about whether the lab fits your oral-history project.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated environment for oral-history research and production.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU’s announcement names an oral history lab among the new Special Collections & Galleries spaces supporting historical research and collaboration.
cards.source_title: GCSU Library puts history on display in new Special Collections facilities
cards.access_notes: Walk-in availability is not stated. Coordinate with Special Collections & Galleries before planning an interview or project session.

cards.title: Study the Book as an Object
cards.subtitle: Rare-material and exhibition space in Special Collections
cards.notes: Contact Special Collections with a focused research question, then follow staff instructions for viewing materials or studying the current display.
cards.short_summary: A controlled setting for close attention to rare books and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The university reports that Russell Library’s renovated Special Collections includes a rare book room with additional exhibit space.
cards.source_title: GCSU Library puts history on display in new Special Collections facilities
cards.access_notes: Rare-material research may be mediated by staff, and exhibit access can vary. Confirm current access with Special Collections & Galleries.

cards.title: Listen with the Score Open
cards.subtitle: Third-floor music study facilities in Russell Library
cards.notes: Bring headphones and the score or listening notes you plan to annotate, then confirm equipment and collection access with library staff.
cards.short_summary: A library setting for attentive listening alongside music coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU’s undergraduate music handbook states that the music collection and listening facilities are housed on Russell Library’s third floor.
cards.access_notes: The handbook identifies the location but does not state walk-in rules. Ask Russell Library about current equipment, collection, and access procedures.

cards.title: Reserve a Room for the Team
cards.subtitle: Bookable group-work spaces in Ina Dillard Russell Library
cards.notes: Open the reservation system before gathering your group, choose an available room sized to the team, and keep the confirmation handy.
cards.short_summary: The library’s official reservable option for contained group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Russell Library’s official page lists study-room reservations among its services, alongside research consultations and technology checkout.
cards.access_notes: Rooms are subject to current reservation availability and library access rules. Use the library’s official study-room reservation service before arriving.
